newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan prosecutors raid Nomura headquarters.
newsitem.headline: Japan prosecutors raid Nomura headquarters.

text.p: Prosecutors entered Nomura Securities Co Ltd's Tokyo headquarters on Tuesday to search its offices as part of investigations into its suspected illegal payments to a corporate client, Reuters reporters on the scene said.
The raid on Japan's biggest brokerage was by both prosecutors and officials of the nation's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC).

The Reuter reporters said about 90 officials in business suits, led by a man with a briefcase, marched through the front doors of the headquarters building in central Tokyo and then locked the doors behind them.
The SESC has been investigating Nomura over its March 6 admission that two directors made discretionary deals banned under Japanese law and funnelled profits to a corporate client.
The client has been linked by the Japanese media to corporate racketeers, known in Japan as "sokaiya", who extort money from companies by threatening to disrupt annual shareholder meetings.

If Nomura's deals are found to violate a commercial code banning payoffs to racketeers, legal action could be taken against the firm, at the request of the SESC. The scandal has already led to the resignation of Nomura's president and an internal investigation by the company.
